# Aritro Saha — Software Engineer 1 at Bristol Myers Squibb

> Official portfolio and project catalog of Aritro Saha, Software Engineer 1 at Bristol Myers Squibb specializing in high-throughput data engineering, cloud systems, and native macOS utilities.

Canonical: https://www.aritro.cloud/
Last updated: 2026-10-26

## Professional Overview
Software Engineer 1 at Bristol Myers Squibb building high-throughput data pipelines, cloud infrastructure, native macOS utilities, and interactive web applications.

Currently serving as a Software Engineer 1 at **Bristol Myers Squibb** (July 2025 – Present), engineering enterprise-scale data pipelines, cloud architecture, and web applications.

## Key Achievements & Honors
- **Hack4Bengal 3.0 Winner**: Eastern India's Largest Hackathon (Winner across 5,000+ applicants).
- **Published Research**: Gesture-controlled computer interfacing and multimodal assistive AI (IJIRT).
- **Open-Source Author**: Published `quarantine-py` fault-tolerance package on PyPI with atomic dead-letter queuing.

## Featured Projects
- [Byakugan Scan](https://www.aritro.cloud/projects/byakugan-scan) — Instant, in-memory screen OCR, QR code, and barcode scanner for macOS built with Swift 6.0 and Apple Vision Framework. Zero telemetry, sub-50ms hotkeys. (Swift 6.0, AppKit, SwiftUI, Apple Vision Framework)
- [SutraKey](https://www.aritro.cloud/projects/sutrakey) — Instant Shift+Select radial pie menu for video, audio, and clean document actions on macOS (Swift 6.0, AppKit, SwiftUI, CGEventTap)
- [OpenWorld Portfolio](https://www.aritro.cloud/projects/openworld-portfolio) — Interactive 2.5D retro Pokémon-inspired open-world developer portfolio set in Pallet Cloud (Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS)
- [Quarantine](https://www.aritro.cloud/projects/quarantine) — Zero-dependency dead-letter queue and fault-tolerance library on PyPI. Wrap Python loops with @quarantine to isolate errors without crashing batch jobs. (Python 3.9+, PyPI, AsyncIO, CLI)
- [Structurify](https://www.aritro.cloud/projects/structurify) — AI-powered SaaS that transforms messy spreadsheet data into a clean master schema (Next.js 14, React, TailwindCSS, Firebase)
- [Luffy Laser Dodge](https://www.aritro.cloud/projects/luffy-laser-dodge) — Interactive 3D reflex game dodging laser beams using actual head movements via webcam (React, Vite, React Three Fiber, Three.js)
- [GlideConnect](https://www.aritro.cloud/projects/glide-connect) — Virtual mouse control platform using MediaPipe hand-gesture recognition and Google Gemini voice assistant. Published in peer-reviewed IJIRT research. (Python 3.9, MediaPipe, OpenCV, Google Gemini API)
- [PAWsitive](https://www.aritro.cloud/projects/pawsitive) — Centralized pet healthcare platform connecting blood donors, vet clinics, and rescue centers (Winner of Hack4Bengal 3.0) (React, Next.js, TypeScript, MongoDB)

## The Developer Arcade (Aritro Games)
An interactive suite of developer-themed browser mini-games engineered in React:
- [Developer Speed Test](https://www.aritro.cloud/play/typing-test) — Test your coding typing speed with this minimalist terminal-style speed test game. Features top programming keywords!
- [Data Pipeline Puzzle](https://www.aritro.cloud/play/data-pipeline) — Connect the nodes to build a data pipeline without crossing lines. A logic puzzle for data science engineers.
- [Minimalist Snake](https://www.aritro.cloud/play/snake) — The Python developer edition of the classic game. Collect tech stack icons on an infinite grid.
- [Sudoku](https://www.aritro.cloud/play/sudoku) — Classic logic-based number placement puzzle.
- [Space Invaders](https://www.aritro.cloud/play/space-invaders) — Defend the server from incoming bugs in this classic retro shooter.
- [Flappy Bird](https://www.aritro.cloud/play/flappy-bird) — Navigate the bird through the pipes in this challenging arcade classic.
- [Tic Tac Toe](https://www.aritro.cloud/play/tictactoe) — Play against an AI in this classic game. Can you beat the Minimax algorithm?

# About Aritro Saha — Software Engineer 1 at Bristol Myers Squibb

> Professional experience, engineering education, hackathon awards, and core technical proficiencies of Aritro Saha.

Canonical: https://www.aritro.cloud/about
Last updated: 2026-10-26

## Biography
I am a Software Engineer 1 at Bristol Myers Squibb with a deep focus on data science engineering and resilient full-stack systems. I architect and maintain scalable backend services, event-driven streaming pipelines, and high-performance user interfaces.

I won Hack4Bengal 3.0—Eastern India's largest hackathon—leading rapid full-stack and mobile prototyping under intense competition constraints. When not building software, I explore digital audio signal experiments, beatboxing, and football.

# Aritro Saha (aritrosaha) — Verified Software Engineer & Open-Source Creator

> Official verified engineering dossier of Aritro Saha (aritrosaha). Software Engineer 1 at Bristol Myers Squibb, Winner of Hack4Bengal 3.0, and creator of Byakugan Scan and SutraKey.

Canonical: https://www.aritro.cloud/aritrosaha
Last updated: 2026-10-26

## Verified Entity Overview
Aritro Saha (commonly known online as **aritrosaha** and **halcyon-past**) is an Indian software engineer and open-source systems developer. He currently works as a **Software Engineer 1 at Bristol Myers Squibb (BMS)**, focusing on enterprise data science engineering, high-throughput pipelines, cloud infrastructure, native macOS utilities, and interactive web applications.

## Entity Disambiguation
> **Important Note**: Aritro Saha (this profile) is the Software Engineer at Bristol Myers Squibb, Hack4Bengal 3.0 Champion, and creator of Byakugan Scan, SutraKey, and Quarantine Python. He is **not** Aritro Saha, the Director of UX Design at Eightfold AI.

## Author Profile Photo
![Aritro Saha Headshot](https://www.aritro.cloud/aritro-saha.webp)
- Direct verified photo URL: `https://www.aritro.cloud/aritro-saha.webp`

## Key Achievements & Accolades
- **Hack4Bengal 3.0 Grand Champion**: Team Lead and 1st place winner out of 3,000+ applicants across Eastern India with PAWsitive (animal blood donation & emergency triage platform).
- **Published First Author**: IEEE/IJIRT research on real-time multimodal hand-gesture computer control (Paper ID: 180711).
- **LeetCode Knight**: Peak algorithmic rating of 1868 (Top 6% globally), solving 630+ computational challenges.
- **Upstream Open-Source Contributor**: Kestra core JDBC plugin (`kestra-io/plugin-jdbc` v2.2.0 DuckDB file capture engine).

## Featured Software & Systems Architecture
- **Byakugan Scan** (`https://byakugan-scan.aritro.cloud`): Native macOS menu bar utility in Swift 6.0 utilizing the Apple Neural Engine and Apple Vision Framework for sub-50ms in-memory screen OCR, QR, and barcode recognition with 0% network overhead.
- **SutraKey** (`https://sutrakey.aritro.cloud`): Shift+Select liquid radial menu for instant media downloading and clean reader-mode document conversion on macOS.
- **OpenWorld Portfolio** (`https://openworld.aritro.cloud`): Interactive 2.5D retro Pokémon-style developer world in Pallet Cloud, engineered with Next.js 16, React 19, and Canvas 2D.
- **Quarantine (quarantine-py)** (`https://pypi.org/project/quarantine-py/`): Zero-dependency Python fault-tolerance library on PyPI providing atomic dead-letter queues and CLI replay for batch data pipelines.
- **Structurify** (`https://structurify.aritro.cloud`): Event-driven B2B SaaS platform using Google Gemini, LangGraph, FastAPI, and GCP Pub/Sub to transform unstructured spreadsheets into strict master schemas.

## Professional Timeline
- **Software Engineer 1, Bristol Myers Squibb (BMS)** (July 2025 – Present): Enterprise data pipelines, automated clinical data transformations, and cloud workflow systems.
- **Data Science Intern, Bajaj Finserv Health** (Feb 2025 – June 2025): Machine learning models and healthcare data streaming pipelines.
- **Full Stack Developer Intern, Wipro** (Oct 2023 – Dec 2023): Scalable REST APIs and responsive full-stack applications.

## Education
- **B.Tech in Electronics & Computer Engineering**, Vellore Institute of Technology, Chennai (2021 – 2025)
- **High School**, Birla Bharati, Kolkata (2021)

# The Arcade — Developer Games by Aritro Saha

> A collection of minimalist, developer-themed browser games built natively in React by Aritro Saha.

Canonical: https://www.aritro.cloud/play
Last updated: 2026-10-26

## The Arcade Overview
The Arcade is a suite of responsive, developer-themed games built natively into Aritro Saha’s portfolio. Engineered in React 19 without third-party game engines, each mini-game demonstrates clean state machines, high-frame-rate requestAnimationFrame loops, or algorithmic AI.

## Games Catalog
- [Developer Speed Test](https://www.aritro.cloud/play/typing-test) — **Available** — Test your coding typing speed with this minimalist terminal-style speed test game. Features top programming keywords! (Tech: React, Custom WPM & Accuracy Engine, Timer Hook)
- [Data Pipeline Puzzle](https://www.aritro.cloud/play/data-pipeline) — **Available** — Connect the nodes to build a data pipeline without crossing lines. A logic puzzle for data science engineers. (Tech: React, BFS Pathfinding, Grid Geometry)
- [Minimalist Snake](https://www.aritro.cloud/play/snake) — **Available** — The Python developer edition of the classic game. Collect tech stack icons on an infinite grid. (Tech: React, HTML5 Canvas / Grid, Game Loop)
- [Sudoku](https://www.aritro.cloud/play/sudoku) — **Available** — Classic logic-based number placement puzzle. (Tech: React, Backtracking Solver, Board Generator)
- [Space Invaders](https://www.aritro.cloud/play/space-invaders) — **Available** — Defend the server from incoming bugs in this classic retro shooter. (Tech: React, requestAnimationFrame Game Loop, Collision Detection)
- [Flappy Bird](https://www.aritro.cloud/play/flappy-bird) — **Available** — Navigate the bird through the pipes in this challenging arcade classic. (Tech: React, 2D Gravity Physics, Box-Model Collision)
- [Tic Tac Toe](https://www.aritro.cloud/play/tictactoe) — **Available** — Play against an AI in this classic game. Can you beat the Minimax algorithm? (Tech: React, Recursive Minimax Algorithm with Alpha-Beta Pruning)

## Algorithmic Highlights
- **Minimax AI**: Unbeatable Alpha-Beta decision tree evaluation in Tic Tac Toe.
- **Pathfinding & Graph Isolation**: Breadth-First Search (BFS) connection validation in Data Pipeline Puzzle.
- **Backtracking Search**: Constraint-satisfaction solving engine in Sudoku.
- **Real-Time WPM & Accuracy**: Microsecond keystroke interval computation in Developer Speed Test.

# Developer Speed Test — Aritro Saha Arcade

> Test your coding typing speed with this minimalist terminal-style speed test game. Features top programming keywords!

Canonical: https://www.aritro.cloud/play/typing-test
Last updated: 2026-10-26

## Game Overview
A retro terminal-style typing speed test tailored specifically for software engineers. Measures Gross and Net Words Per Minute (WPM), character accuracy, and keystroke timing using syntax snippets from JavaScript, Python, Swift, and Rust.

## Technical Implementation
- **Architecture**: React, Custom WPM & Accuracy Engine, Timer Hook
- **Status**: Available
- **Controls**: Optimized for desktop keyboard & mouse as well as mobile touch screens.

## How to Play
Access the live interactive playable game at https://www.aritro.cloud/play/typing-test.

# Data Pipeline Puzzle — Aritro Saha Arcade

> Connect the nodes to build a data pipeline without crossing lines. A logic puzzle for data science engineers.

Canonical: https://www.aritro.cloud/play/data-pipeline
Last updated: 2026-10-26

## Game Overview
An interactive graph connectivity puzzle modeled after distributed data pipelines (like Spark, Airflow, and Databricks). Connect ingestion sources to storage sinks without allowing pipelines to overlap or deadlock.

## Technical Implementation
- **Architecture**: React, BFS Pathfinding, Grid Geometry
- **Status**: Available
- **Controls**: Optimized for desktop keyboard & mouse as well as mobile touch screens.

# Byakugan Scan — by Aritro Saha

> Instant, in-memory screen OCR, QR code, and barcode scanner for macOS built with Swift 6.0 and Apple Vision Framework. Zero telemetry, sub-50ms hotkeys.

Canonical: https://www.aritro.cloud/projects/byakugan-scan
Last updated: 2026-10-26

## Project Overview
Byakugan Scan is a native macOS menu bar utility for instant, in-memory screen OCR, QR code, and barcode recognition. Unlike conventional screenshot OCR tools that write temporary image files to disk and trigger Spotlight or media analysis daemons, Byakugan Scan captures selected screen regions directly into NSPasteboard memory as a CGImage buffer and processes them on the Apple Neural Engine in under 50ms—with zero temporary files, zero network calls, and zero external Swift package dependencies.

## Key Engineering Features
- Zero-Disk In-Memory Pipeline: Captures screen selections straight into RAM via NSPasteboard and runs Apple Vision requests (VNRecognizeTextRequest and VNDetectBarcodesRequest) on the Neural Engine in under 50ms.
- 60/120Hz Custom AppKit Overlay: Smooth multi-display selection reticle with customizable theme accents (Byakugan Violet, Tenseigan Cyan, Sharingan Crimson, Sage Emerald, Nine-Tails Amber) and adjustable backdrop dimming.
- Multi-Language OCR & Barcode Decoding: Supports automatic language detection across 13+ languages alongside QR, MicroQR, EAN-8/13, UPC-E, Code 128/39/93, PDF417, Aztec, and Data Matrix symbologies.
- Floating HUD & Contextual Actions: Frosted-glass HUD toast displaying character/word counts and one-click actions to open URLs, compose emails, or dial phone numbers without cluttering Notification Center.
- URL Scheme Automation & Local History: Deep-link automation via byakugan:// for Raycast, Alfred, and Shortcuts, plus a searchable local scan history with category filters and pinning.

# SutraKey — by Aritro Saha

> Instant Shift+Select radial pie menu for video, audio, and clean document actions on macOS

Canonical: https://www.aritro.cloud/projects/sutrakey
Last updated: 2026-10-26

## Project Overview
SutraKey (सूत्र) is a native, lightweight macOS utility designed as an invisible thread connecting text selection to instant media and document actions. When you hold Shift and select any URL or text, an under-cursor radial pie menu smoothly appears, letting you download videos, extract high-bitrate audio, pull clean subtitles, scrape gallery images, or generate ad-free reader-mode PDFs directly into ~/Downloads—with 0% idle CPU and zero background bloat.

## Key Engineering Features
- Exclusive Shift + Select Trigger: Uses CGEventTap with bitwise modifier evaluation (NSEvent.modifierFlags) ensuring the radial menu only summons when Shift is exclusively held, completely avoiding interference with standard Command, Option, or Control shortcuts.
- 60 FPS Under-Cursor Radial Menu: A frameless, transparent, non-activating NSPanel with 5 radial slices (Video MP4 via yt-dlp+ffmpeg, 320kbps MP3 Audio, Clean Subtitles, High-Res Image Gallery, Reader-Mode Clean PDF via offscreen WKWebView) and a dead-zone center for instant flick-cancelling.
- Ephemeral Menu Bar Presence: Remains 100% invisible when idle; dynamically surfaces a monochrome progress indicator in the macOS menu bar only during active conversion tasks and auto-vanishes 1.5s after completion.
- Frosted Glass Toast HUD: Native floating status notifications with macOS .ultraThinMaterial blur displaying transfer speeds, ETA, and one-click "Show in Finder" buttons.
- Strict Sandboxed Output & Security: Strictly confines all downloads to ~/Downloads with automatic path-traversal guards (--no-exec, --restrict-filenames).

# Quarantine — by Aritro Saha

> Zero-dependency dead-letter queue and fault-tolerance library on PyPI. Wrap Python loops with @quarantine to isolate errors without crashing batch jobs.

Canonical: https://www.aritro.cloud/projects/quarantine
Last updated: 2026-10-26

## Project Overview
quarantine is an open-source, zero-dependency Python library that brings dead-letter queue resilience to regular loops and batch data pipelines. When processing thousands of records (e.g., CSV ingestion, scraping, API syncing), an unexpected exception at item #5,247 no longer crashes the entire multi-hour run. quarantine safely isolates the failing item, captures the error and full execution state to disk, and keeps the loop running.

## Key Engineering Features
- Zero-Crash Decorators: Wrap any sync or async function with @quarantine or iterate with shield() to set aside failures without interrupting the pipeline.
- Atomic On-Disk Isolation: Serializes failed inputs, exceptions, and full tracebacks atomically to disk (.quarantine/) without requiring external message brokers.
- Surgical Replays & Interactive Debugging: Rerun only failed items using quarantine retry or drop straight into pdb with the exact failing input using quarantine debug.
- Circuit Breakers & Sensitive Redaction: Automatic circuit breaker tripping via halt_after to prevent cascading external outages, plus built-in key/regex redaction for secrets.
- Local Web UI & Observability: Built-in CLI commands and a local web dashboard to inspect tracebacks, track recovery stats, and integrate into CI/CD pipelines.

## Technologies & Architecture
- Python 3.9+
- PyPI
- AsyncIO
- CLI
- Dead-Letter Queue
- Fault Tolerance
- Pytest

## Verified Links & Source Code
- **GitHub Repository**: [https://github.com/halcyon-past/quarantine](https://github.com/halcyon-past/quarantine)
- **Live Website / Deployment**: [https://pypi.org/project/quarantine-py/](https://pypi.org/project/quarantine-py/)
- **Documentation**: [https://quarantine-py.aritro.cloud](https://quarantine-py.aritro.cloud)

# Building Sub-50ms Zero-Disk Screen OCR with Swift 6 & Apple Vision Framework — by Aritro Saha

> How to architect an in-memory macOS screen OCR pipeline using Swift 6, NSPasteboard, and Apple Vision VNRecognizeTextRequest with zero temporary disk writes.

Canonical: https://www.aritro.cloud/blog/swift-vision-ocr-apple-neural-engine
Last updated: 2026-10-20

> Category: macOS Engineering | Published: 2026-10-20 | Reading Time: 6 min read

How to architect an in-memory macOS screen OCR pipeline using Swift 6, NSPasteboard, and Apple Vision VNRecognizeTextRequest with zero temporary disk writes.

## The Disk Bottleneck in Traditional Screenshot OCR Tools

Most conventional macOS screen OCR tools execute a naive three-step pipeline: invoke `screencapture` to persist a temporary PNG file in `/tmp/`, trigger an OCR process on that file, and delete the file. This creates immediate I/O latency, triggers Spotlight indexing daemons, and incurs unnecessary NVMe SSD write wear. In high-frequency workflows, disk latency alone accounts for 80–120ms of overhead.

## Capturing Directly into In-Memory Pasteboard Buffers

By leveraging macOS AppKit and `NSPasteboard` memory streams, screen selections are captured straight into RAM as an uncompressed `CGImage` buffer. Using Swift 6 strict concurrency checks, we transfer this frame directly into Apple Vision framework without a single byte touching disk:

```swift
func captureSelectedRegion(rect: CGRect) -> CGImage? {
    guard let displayId = CGMainDisplayID() as CGDirectDisplayID? else { return nil }
    return CGDisplayCreateImage(displayId, rect: rect)
}
```

Because zero temporary files are generated, the pipeline executes with sub-millisecond I/O footprint and leaves no residual telemetry or cached artifacts on disk.

## Hardware Acceleration via the Apple Neural Engine (ANE)

The optical recognition phase is executed using `VNRecognizeTextRequest`. By configuring the request with `recognitionLevel = .accurate` and directing execution to the Apple Neural Engine compute device (`.cpuAndNeuralEngine`), inference latency is slashed to under 35ms on M-series Apple Silicon:

```swift
let request = VNRecognizeTextRequest { request, error in
    guard let observations = request.results as? [VNRecognizedTextObservation] else { return }
    let recognizedStrings = observations.compactMap { $0.topCandidates(1).first?.string }
    DispatchQueue.main.async {
        NSPasteboard.general.clearContents()
        NSPasteboard.general.setString(recognizedStrings.join(separator: "\n"), forType: .string)
    }
}
request.usesLanguageCorrection = true
```

The result is true sub-50ms latency from hotkey press to text in clipboard.

## Key Engineering Takeaways for macOS Utilities

1. **Avoid File I/O for Ephemeral Data**: Memory buffers through `CGImage` and `NSPasteboard` offer 10x lower latency than temporary files.
2. **Target the Apple Neural Engine Explicitly**: Modern Apple Silicon provides dedicated ANE compute units that leave CPU cores free for UI responsiveness.
3. **Embrace Swift 6 Strict Concurrency**: Protect shared state in background menu bar utilities by marking capture pipelines with `@MainActor` or isolated actors.

## Tags & Topics
`#Swift 6` `#macOS` `#Apple Vision` `#Neural Engine` `#OCR` `#Performance`

**Aritro Saha** — Software Engineer 1 at Bristol Myers Squibb. Specialized in distributed systems, Apple Silicon engineering, and resilient batch pipelines.

# Architecting Zero-Crash Batch Data Pipelines with Python Dead-Letter Queues (DLQ) — by Aritro Saha

> Eliminate pipeline crashes at record #5,247. A deep dive into implementing fault-tolerant Python loops, atomic error serialization, and surgical CLI replays.

Canonical: https://www.aritro.cloud/blog/python-dead-letter-queue-batch-pipelines
Last updated: 2026-10-24

> Category: Data Engineering | Published: 2026-10-24 | Reading Time: 8 min read

Eliminate pipeline crashes at record #5,247. A deep dive into implementing fault-tolerant Python loops, atomic error serialization, and surgical CLI replays.

## The Fatal Flaw of Unbounded Batch Loops

Every data engineer has experienced this nightmare: a batch job ingesting 100,000 records from an upstream ERP or API crashes at record #84,219 due to an unexpected null byte or schema anomaly. The entire 4-hour batch fails, uncommitted database transactions roll back, and on-call engineers must write throwaway scripts to figure out which record broke the process.

## Implementing the In-Process Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ) Pattern

While enterprise message brokers like Apache Kafka and AWS SQS provide dead-letter queues, standalone Python batch scripts, Databricks ETL notebooks, and scraping workers traditionally lack built-in DLQ mechanisms. 

To solve this, we architected **quarantine** (available on PyPI as `quarantine-py`). It wraps batch loops with atomic isolation:

```python
from quarantine import quarantine

@quarantine(halt_after=10, redact_keys=["password", "ssn"])
def process_record(record: dict) -> None:
    # Business logic that might raise unpredictable exceptions
    transform_and_insert(record)
```

When an error occurs, the function does not crash the loop. Instead, the failing input, timestamp, exception type, and full traceback are atomically serialized to an isolated `.quarantine/` directory on disk.

## Circuit Breakers & Sensitive Credential Redaction

A resilient dead-letter queue must distinguish between occasional bad records and systemic upstream outages. 

1. **Circuit Breakers (`halt_after`)**: If an upstream database goes offline, isolating 10,000 consecutive items into the DLQ is counterproductive. Quarantine trips a circuit breaker and terminates cleanly if consecutive failures exceed a threshold.
2. **Zero Telemetry Leakage**: Before serializing state to disk, automated regex and key-based masking scrubs sensitive keys (e.g. passwords, API tokens, medical identifiers) to remain HIPAA and GDPR compliant.

## Surgical Replay and Debugging Workflows

Isolating failures is only half the battle; recovery is where developer velocity compounds. With a dedicated CLI inspector:

```bash
# Inspect quarantined items with formatted tracebacks
quarantine list

# Rerun only the failed records through fixed logic
quarantine retry --all

# Drop straight into pdb post-mortem debugger with the exact failing payload
quarantine debug <record_id>
```

By decoupling error handling from core batch pipelines, developers achieve resilient, self-healing batch processing without external infrastructure dependencies.

## Tags & Topics
`#Python` `#Data Engineering` `#Fault Tolerance` `#Dead-Letter Queue` `#Architecture` `#PyPI`

## Author Profile
**Aritro Saha** — Software Engineer 1 at Bristol Myers Squibb. Specialized in distributed systems, Apple Silicon engineering, and resilient batch pipelines.

# Achieving 0ms Perceived Navigation in Vite & React 19 with W3C Speculation Rules — by Aritro Saha

> How to upgrade traditional SPAs into instant-navigation platforms using modern W3C Speculation Rules, React 19 SSG prerendering, and Core Web Vitals optimization.

Canonical: https://www.aritro.cloud/blog/instant-navigation-speculation-rules-vite-ssg
Last updated: 2026-10-28

> Category: Web Architecture | Published: 2026-10-28 | Reading Time: 5 min read

How to upgrade traditional SPAs into instant-navigation platforms using modern W3C Speculation Rules, React 19 SSG prerendering, and Core Web Vitals optimization.

## Beyond Traditional Client-Side Routing

In standard React Single Page Applications (SPAs), internal page transitions require executing JavaScript route matchers, loading code-split chunks, and updating DOM nodes. While fast, transitions still incur 50–150ms of main thread delay and can trigger Interaction to Next Paint (INP) degradations.

## The Power of the W3C Speculation Rules API

The modern W3C Speculation Rules API introduces declarative background prerendering at the browser engine level. Unlike legacy `<link rel="prerender">`, speculation rules allow structured JSON configurations specifying match patterns, exclusion rules, and eagerness levels:

```html
<script type="speculationrules">
{
  "prerender": [
    {
      "where": {
        "and": [
          { "href_matches": "/*" },
          { "not": { "href_matches": "/assets/*" } },
          { "not": { "href_matches": "/api/*" } }
        ]
      },
      "eagerness": "moderate"
    }
  ]
}
</script>
```

With `"eagerness": "moderate"`, Chromium browsers detect when a user hovers or moves their cursor toward an internal link and silently render the destination page in an offscreen process.

## Synergy with React 19 Static Site Generation (SSG)

Speculation rules deliver maximum impact when paired with pre-rendered static HTML routes. Because every route on this site is pre-rendered at build time with full HTML, CSS, and hydration scripts:
1. The background browser process receives instant 200 OK responses from the edge CDN.
2. The page is completely painted before the user clicks.
3. Upon clicking, the browser swaps the background document into view instantly, achieving a true **0ms perceived navigation duration**.

## Core Web Vitals Impact and Safety Rules

1. **Guarding Analytics & Side-Effects**: Use `document.prerendering` checks in analytics scripts to avoid logging phantom pageviews before user activation.
2. **Preserving BFCache**: Avoid `unload` and `beforeunload` event listeners, ensuring that both Forward-Back Cache (BFCache) and speculative prerendering operate at peak efficiency.
3. **Granular Asset Exclusion**: Always exclude heavy asset downloads, audio streams, and API routes from speculation rules matching.
